subject.title: [Feature]: Safe model routing — shadow-mode candidate admission and audit trail for managed tasks (Phase 0-1)

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a narrow, generic plugin-SDK observation/admission seam for task-specific fallback auditing, or keep fallback audit policy outside the core product for now?
rationale: Current main has structured fallback observability but no established public contract for task capability policy, durable route auditing, or a bundled safe-routing feature. Choosing that public boundary and whether it merits core support requires maintainer product and SDK ownership intent.

options.title: Design a minimal generic seam
options.body: Sponsor a focused RFC that proves the missing event data and lifecycle point, keeps task policy and SQLite ownership external, and avoids adding a bundled feature or mode until the seam is accepted.

options.title: External plugin experiment first
options.body: Build the policy and reporting as an external code plugin using existing fallback decision telemetry where possible, then propose only the demonstrated missing SDK hook.

options.title: Park the direction
options.body: Leave current fallback observability unchanged until a broader supported managed-task product surface makes capability admission a confirmed priority.

recommendation.title: Design a minimal generic seam
recommendation.body: Sponsor a focused RFC that proves the missing event data and lifecycle point, keeps task policy and SQLite ownership external, and avoids adding a bundled feature or mode until the seam is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent review and implementation history ties this person most directly to fallback semantics and the needed plugin-boundary decision.
